    The converse of Corollary 4.15: A ≅ A₀ implies that A is standard #

    scalar-normalization.tex: "Conversely an isomorphism A ≅ A₀ gives an equivalence F : ind(mod A) → C, possibly permuting labels. Since C is generated in degree one with homogeneous relations, gr_J C = C. Thus gr F is a graded automorphism of C with the same permutation. Applying (gr F)⁻¹ after F gives the required object-preserving equivalence."

    An isomorphism ψ : A ≅ A₀ makes the evaluated modules M_x of C = k(Γ_A) into indecomposable A-modules, which identifies C with ind(mod A) up to a permutation σ of the labels (Φ). Under Φ the radical powers of ind(mod A) are the morphisms of degree at least m of C (gr_J C = C, MeshRadical). Deviation: instead of correcting F by (gr F)⁻¹, the degree-one parts of the arrow representatives are taken as lifts; their mesh errors are of degree two and lie in J³, so they vanish, and the filtered normal form (Lifts.functor) gives the object-preserving equivalence (isStandard_of_algEquiv).
